scenes.setting: The Harvest Church turned plague ward: Emlyn brews fifty doses and hands them out with contempt beside a bishop who takes in unbelievers because 'they are also lives' — and then reveals that the psychological cue only ever made him come back to the cathedral
scenes.text_anchor: “The only effect of the psychological cue was to make me return to the cathedral?”

scenes.setting: New Year's Eve at 2 Daffodil Street: tickets booked for the 3rd of January, talk of Backlund's new laws and its desperate factories — and a table laid with three sets of cutlery, three plates, three cups
scenes.text_anchor: Three cups. One for beer, two for ginger beer.

scenes.setting: A newspaper counting 21,000 dead in the fog and 40,000 more to plague sits in the lounge; Audrey puts on her elegant smile, takes the queen's hand before the guests, and is presented to society as fireworks break over the window

A new cemetery on East Borough's edge: Old Kohler's niche has no photograph, no epitaph, not even a name — so Klein carves one, 'He was a good worker. He had a wife, a son, and a daughter. He worked hard to live.' — and leaves Daisy's case anonymously to Reporter Mike rather than touch her life himself

The locomotive carries hopeful workers into the Land of Hope; on the platform Benson and Melissa feel a gaze and see only a black-haired gentleman in gold-rimmed glasses, who walks past them into the departure station. 'It was the best of times, it was the worst of times.' (End of Volume 2 — Faceless)
scenes.text_anchor: It was the best of times, it was the worst of times.
